Thoughts I see the inpatient table is already at the claim/visit level.non-inpatient is not. we need to get it down to that granularity. We will need to add in line_count column in order to capture the number of raw lines used to reconstruct the claim. Line_count for inpatient will just be 1. 

### Step 0A. Counting total patients vs. patients patients with valid hospice admission

```{r}
cat("STEP 0: Counting total patients and hospice admission...\n")

population_hospice_counts <- DatabaseConnector::querySql(
  con,
  paste0(
"
WITH hospice_admission_patients AS (

    /* Patients with hospice admission in non-inpatient claims */
    SELECT DISTINCT
        patient_id
    FROM ", komodo_schema, ".non_inpatient_events
    WHERE patient_id IS NOT NULL
      AND UPPER(TRIM(bill_type_code)) IN (
            '81A','82A',
            '812','822',
            '811','821'
          )

    UNION

    /* Patients with hospice admission in inpatient claims */
    SELECT DISTINCT
        patient_id
    FROM ", komodo_schema, ".inpatient_events
    WHERE patient_id IS NOT NULL
      AND UPPER(TRIM(bill_type_code)) IN (
            '81A','82A',
            '812','822',
            '811','821'
          )
)

SELECT

    COUNT(DISTINCT d.patient_id)
        AS total_patients,

    COUNT(
        DISTINCT CASE
            WHEN h.patient_id IS NOT NULL
            THEN d.patient_id
        END
    ) AS patients_with_hospice_admission,

    COUNT(
        DISTINCT CASE
            WHEN h.patient_id IS NULL
            THEN d.patient_id
        END
    ) AS patients_without_hospice_admission

FROM ", komodo_schema, ".patient_demographics d

LEFT JOIN hospice_admission_patients h
    ON d.patient_id = h.patient_id;
"
  )
)
names(population_hospice_counts) <-
  tolower(names(population_hospice_counts))
print(population_hospice_counts)
cat("STEP 0 COMPLETE\n")
```


### STEP 0B Granularity Check on Non-inpatient table 

this was a check to **confirm structure for non-inpatient**. This confirms that claim identity should be patient_id and utilization id as hospice information may be split across those lines.


### Step 1 Checking quality for preprocessing done on DBeaver 
This was the process done for DBeaver tables:
* CREATE batch_keys
* CREATE batch_lines
* CREATE batch_core
* CREATE batch_events
* Quality Check everything
* INSERT INTO hospice_nonip_events
* verify that year's rows are now permanent
* DROP:
       * batch_keys
       * batch_lines
       * batch_core
       * batch_events
* next year repeat
Finalized rows for in-patient table:
    patient_id,
    utilization_id,
    claim_source,
    event_date,
    event_date_source,
    bill_type_code,
    level_code,

    revenue_codes,

    service_area_type,

    service_date,
    service_to_date,
    line_count,
    first_line_number,
    last_line_number,
    line_numbers
I then added in a command for each table to be based on hospice admission so going off of bill types: 81A, 82A, 812, 822, 821, and 811. Finally, when merging the two tables together it was very simple and chose it to be the earliest hospice admission entry date chosen per patients (.hospice_candidates). We will create a new column that has closed T/F to determine whether a patient was closed a year back prior to admission for both RX and MX.
                    * TRUE  = patient has continuous MX CLOSED AND RX CLOSED
                            covering the entire 12 months before hospice entry
                    
                    * FALSE = one or both are not continuously closed for that full year
After age identification for 50 and up upon hospice entrance. I made a new table for the final candidates being :
.hospice_f_candidates.I then added in a column based on what the protocol wanted and had it be medicaid_primary if it was someone's primary insurance. for MEDICAID.

### Step 2 HIV identification 

To start I made two new columns for this table of .hospice_f_candidates. hiv_status being True or False (boolean) and hiv_most_recent_date this will be the most recent date of HIV being identified through prescription medication (not including lamivudine as it treats Hep B).

```{r}
# Reuse Nemo's lookup/import helpers. NOT using ohdsilab as it sucks
source("1_configure_clinical_metrics.R")
candidate_table <- paste0(
  write_schema,
  ".hospice_f_candidates"
)
#load nemos HIV diagnosis lookup 
hiv_lookup <- read_lookup_csv(
  file.path(
    "Clinical Metric Look Up Tables",
    "0.6_hiv_diagnosis_lookup.csv"
  )
)
hiv_codes <- unique(
  data.frame(
    dx_code = hiv_lookup$match_value[
      toupper(hiv_lookup$metric) == "HIV" &
      hiv_lookup$code_system == "ICD10CM" &

      !is.na(hiv_lookup$match_value)
```

We merge the tables. Route 3 is doing two jobs simultaneously:
1. Finding new HIV-positive people who failed Routes 1 and 2.
2. Providing a potentially more recent HIV evidence date for people who already passed Routes 1 or 2.


My thoughts based on what the protocol said:
I would exclude standalone lamivudine products, regardless of whether that particular formulation is commonly used for HIV or HBV. That means regular EPIVIR should also be excluded for this algorithm because its active drug is still lamivudine. FDA labeling confirms EPIVIR is lamivudine for HIV treatment, while EPIVIR-HBV is the lower-dose HBV product. I still saw epivir recommended to sever HEP B.

### Pharmacy Based HIV identification - medication exclusions 

Route 3 requires at least two distinct qualifying antiretroviral medication fill dates. Medications with alternative indications were excluded as independent evidence of HIV infection to reduce potential misclassification.Also it is for PAID pharmacy transactions with FINAL o STANDALONE transaction status 

Excluded medications:

Standalone lamivudine: LAMIVUDINE, LAMIVUDINE HBV, EPIVIR HBV.

Standalone tenofovir: TENOFOVIR, TENOFOVIR ALEFENAMIDE, TENOFOVIR ALAFENAMIDE, TENOFOVIR DISOPROXIL FUMARATE, VEMLIDY, VIREAD.

Standalone ritonavir: RITONAVIR, NORVIR.

HIV prevention or potentially dual-use medications: APRETUDE, YEZTUGO, DESCOVY, TRUVADA, VOCABRIA, EMTRICITABINE-TENOFOVIR DISOP, EMTRICITABINE/TENOFOVIR.

Retained medications:

EPIVIR (HIV-1 treatment formulation, distinct from EPIVIR HBV).
EPZICOM.
ABACAVIR-LAMIVUDINE.
ABACAVIR-LAMIVUDINE-ZIDOVUDINE.
DOLUTEGRAVIR-LAMIVUDINE.
LAMIVUDINE-ZIDOVUDINE.
LOPINAVIR-RITONAVIR.
Other qualifying combination HIV treatment products and there is a longer excel document. 

Important distinction: These exclusions apply to pharmacy-based HIV cohort identification, not automatically to antiretroviral therapy (ART) adherence measurement. Appropriate dual-use medications and pharmacokinetic boosters may contribute to ART coverage among patients already identified as HIV-positive.



What I would write in methods section of paper:

Pharmacy-based HIV identification required at least two distinct pre-hospice fill dates for medications contained in the study HIV medication reference. Standalone lamivudine products were excluded because lamivudine may also be prescribed for hepatitis B; combination antiretroviral products containing lamivudine were retained


**route 3: medication reference **
```{r}
library(readxl)

# Read the HIV medication reference file
hiv_drugs <- read_excel("HIVDrugAbbrev.xlsx")
# Reduce to one row per unique medication name
hiv_drug_lookup <- unique(
  data.frame(
    drug_name = toupper(trimws(hiv_drugs$DrugName)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
)
# Remove blanks / missing names
hiv_drug_lookup <- hiv_drug_lookup[
  !is.na(hiv_drug_lookup$drug_name) &
    hiv_drug_lookup$drug_name != "",
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
# Check the unique medication list
print(hiv_drug_lookup)

nrow(hiv_drug_lookup)
# should be 139
```

cohort identification flag 
```{r}
hiv_drug_lookup$identify_hiv <- TRUE

# Drugs that should NOT independently establish HIV status
hiv_identification_exclusions <- c(
  # Cabotegravir:
  # APRETUDE = PrEP
  # VOCABRIA can be treatment OR PrEP
  # generic CABOTEGRAVIR is therefore ambiguous
  "APRETUDE",
  "VOCABRIA",
  "CABOTEGRAVIR",
  # Lamivudine / HBV ambiguity
  "LAMIVUDINE",
  "LAMIVUDINE HBV",
  "EPIVIR HBV",
  # Mentor-specified exclusions
  "APRETUDE",
  "YEZTUGO",
  # Standalone tenofovir products
  "TENOFOVIR",
  "TENOFOVIR ALEFENAMIDE",
  "TENOFOVIR ALAFENAMIDE",
  "TENOFOVIR DISOPROXIL FUMARATE",
  "VEMLIDY",
  "VIREAD",
  #FTC + TAF again HIV treatment or prep 
  "DESCOVY",
  "EMTRICITABINE-TENOFOVIR ALAFENAMIDE",
  "EMTRICITABINE-TENOFOVIR ALEFENAMIDE",
  #FTC + TDF can be HIV treatment or prep 
  "TRUVADA",
  "EMTRICITABINE-TENOFOVIR DISOPROXIL FUMARATE",
  # Standalone ritonavir
  "RITONAVIR",
  "NORVIR"
)
# Change only those drugs to FALSE
hiv_drug_lookup$identify_hiv[
  hiv_drug_lookup$drug_name %in% hiv_identification_exclusions
] <- FALSE
#see everything excluded from route 3
hiv_drug_lookup[
  hiv_drug_lookup$identify_hiv == FALSE,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
```

## CFI 
Load Nemos 3 lookup pieces and put them into a permanent Redshift lookup tables. We then load the unifed diagnosis rules and retain the active CFI and Gagne ICD-10 rules. 
```{r}
source("1_configure_clinical_metrics.R")
lookup_dir <- "Clinical Metric Look Up Tables"
# CFI + GAGNE DIAGNOSIS LOOKUP
diagnosis_lookup <- read.csv(
  file.path(lookup_dir, "0.6_unified_diagnosis_rule_lookup.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

diagnosis_lookup$metric <- toupper(diagnosis_lookup$metric)
diagnosis_lookup$match_type <- tolower(diagnosis_lookup$match_type)

diagnosis_lookup <- diagnosis_lookup[
  diagnosis_lookup$code_system == "ICD10CM" &
    diagnosis_lookup$metric %in% c("CFI","GAGNE") &
    toupper(diagnosis_lookup$final_match_after_flattening) == "TRUE",
]
```

Now CFI procedure rules:
```{r}
# CFI PROCEDURE LOOKUP
procedure_lookup <- read.csv(
  file.path(lookup_dir, "0.6_cfi_procedure_lookup.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
procedure_lookup$metric <- toupper(procedure_lookup$metric)
procedure_lookup$match_type <- tolower(procedure_lookup$match_type)
procedure_lookup <- procedure_lookup[
  procedure_lookup$metric == "CFI" &
    procedure_lookup$code_system %in% c("CPT_HCPCS","CPTHCPCS") &
    procedure_lookup$match_type == "range",
]

```

Now the CFI weights:
```{r}
# CFI WEIGHTS
cfi_weights <- read.csv(
  file.path(lookup_dir, "0.6_cfi_weight_lookup.csv"),

)
cfi_weights <- cfi_weights[
  toupper(cfi_weights$metric) == "CFI",
]
cfi_weights$disease_number <- as.integer(cfi_weights$disease_number)
cfi_weights$weight <- as.numeric(cfi_weights$weight)
```

### CCW-30 condition count
```{r}
ccw_lookup_dir <- file.path(
  "Clinical Metric Look Up Tables",
  "CCW30"
)

ccw_lookup <- read.csv(
  file.path(ccw_lookup_dir, "0.6_ccw30_diagnosis_lookup.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

ccw_lookup$match_type <- tolower(ccw_lookup$match_type)
ccw_lookup$rule_type <- tolower(ccw_lookup$rule_type)

ccw_inclusions <- ccw_lookup[
  ccw_lookup$rule_type == "inclusion",
]

table(ccw_inclusions$qualification_group)
table(ccw_inclusions$match_type)

```

These are the CCW propertes that Nemo expects. Nemo’s qualification logic is: group 1 needs inpatient evidence; groups 2–3 need inpatient or $\geq $2 distinct outpatient dates; group 4 needs outpatient; groups 5–6 need any setting.

First we upload only the inclusion lookup once from rstudio 
```{r}
ccw_upload <- ccw_inclusions[
  c(
    "lookup_version",
    "condition_name",
    "condition_name_long",
    "ccw_condition_id",
    "qualification_group",
    "dx_code"
  )
]

DatabaseConnector::executeSql(
  con,
"
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS work_rohanramirez_a299.ccw30_lookup;

CREATE TABLE work_rohanramirez_a299.ccw30_lookup (
    lookup_version VARCHAR(128),
    condition_name VARCHAR(64),
    condition_name_long VARCHAR(256),
    ccw_condition_id VARCHAR(128),
    qualification_group INTEGER,
    dx_code VARCHAR(64)
)
DISTSTYLE ALL
SORTKEY(dx_code);
"
)

ccw_upload$qualification_group <- as.character(
  ccw_upload$qualification_group
)

insert_data_frame(
  con,
  "work_rohanramirez_a299.ccw30_lookup",
  names(ccw_upload),
  ccw_upload,
  numeric_columns = "qualification_group"
)
```

```{r}
DatabaseConnector::querySql(

SELECT
    qualification_group,
    COUNT(*) AS codes
FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.ccw30_lookup
GROUP BY qualification_group
ORDER BY qualification_group;
"
)
```


What I did on R was count how many diagnosis code rows in Nemos CCW lookup belonged to each qualification group. Then I used the code rows to make sure they map into 30 CCW conditions with each condition belonging to one qualification group.

So for example, group 2 having 1,914 codes does NOT mean there are 1,914 CCW conditions. It means that the conditions governed by qualification rule 2 collectively have 1,914 ICD diagnosis codes that can identify them.

The qualification group tells us what evidence a a ptient needs before we count that CCW condition as present:
* group 1 - at least 1 inpatient diagnosis 
* group 2- at least 1 inpatient diagnosis or $\geq$ 2 distinct outpatient dates 
* group 3- same as group 2
* group 4- at least 1 outpatient diagnosis 
* group 5- at least 1 diagnosis either setting 
* group 6- at least 1 diagnosis either setting 

So at the end when we see a patient with like 7 ccw condtion count it means they met the required claims based qualification criteria for 7 out of 30 CCW conditions. So they could have hundreds of claims/codes contributing to those 7 conditions 

Nemo creates 2 CCW outputs while we only carried the one variable i need. His code does 3 jobs. 

ccw30_conditions_long_table
- one row per QUALIFIED patient-condition

ccw30_indicators_table
- one row per patient + 30 individual 0/1 condition flags
   - ccw_cancer
   - ccw_condition_count

ccw30_counts_table
- stripped-down table containing only the total condition count


### Gagne + CFI Summary 
```{r}
clinical_summary <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
WITH gagne AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS n_patients,
        AVG(gagne_score) AS mean_gagne,
        STDDEV(gagne_score) AS sd_gagne,
        MEDIAN(gagne_score) AS median_gagne,
        MIN(gagne_score) AS min_gagne,
        MAX(gagne_score) AS max_gagne,
        SUM(CASE WHEN gagne_score IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_gagne
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_f_candidates
),
cfi AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(cfi_score) AS mean_cfi,
        STDDEV(cfi_score) AS sd_cfi,
        MEDIAN(cfi_score) AS median_cfi,
        MIN(cfi_score) AS min_cfi,
        MAX(cfi_score) AS max_cfi,
        SUM(CASE WHEN cfi_score IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_cfi
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_f_candidates
)
SELECT
    g.n_patients,
    g.mean_gagne,
    g.sd_gagne,
    g.median_gagne,
    g.min_gagne,
    g.max_gagne,
    g.missing_gagne,
    c.mean_cfi,
    c.sd_cfi,
    c.median_cfi,
    c.min_cfi,
    c.max_cfi,
    c.missing_cfi
FROM gagne g
CROSS JOIN cfi c
")
clinical_summary
```

### Frailty level query 
CFI $<$ 0.25   is Robust
0.25 to $<$ 0.35 is Prefrail
CFI $\geq$ 0.35   is Frail
```{r}
frailty_summary <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT
        frailty_level,
        COUNT(*) AS n,
        ROUND(
            100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (),
            2
        ) AS pct
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_f_candidates
    GROUP BY frailty_level
    ORDER BY n DESC

)
```

```{r}
DBI::dbExecute(
  con,
```

```{r}
  /*DROP TABLE IF EXISTS work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_art_name_bridge; */

  CREATE TABLE work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_art_name_bridge
  DISTSTYLE ALL
  SORTKEY(match_name) AS

  SELECT DISTINCT
      drug_name AS match_name,
      drug_name AS canonical_drug_name,
      'CANONICAL' AS mapping_source
  FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_art_component_lookup

  UNION

      a.alias_name AS match_name,
      a.DrugName AS canonical_drug_name,
      'EXISTING_ALIAS' AS mapping_source
  FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_drug_alias a
  INNER JOIN (
      SELECT DISTINCT drug_name
      FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_art_component_lookup
  ) e
      ON a.DrugName = e.drug_name
  WHERE a.alias_name IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(a.alias_name) <> '';
  "
)
```

```{r}
DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
```

```{r}
  WITH no_art AS (
```

```{r}
),
routes AS (
    SELECT
        n.patient_id,
        CASE
            WHEN COALESCE(d.inpatient_pass, 0) = 1
             AND COALESCE(d.outpatient_hiv_dates, 0) >= 2
             AND COALESCE(r.pharmacy_pass, 0) = 1
                THEN 'INPATIENT + OUTPATIENT + PHARMACY'
            WHEN COALESCE(d.inpatient_pass, 0) = 1
             AND COALESCE(d.outpatient_hiv_dates, 0) >= 2
                THEN 'INPATIENT + OUTPATIENT'
            WHEN COALESCE(d.inpatient_pass, 0) = 1
             AND COALESCE(r.pharmacy_pass, 0) = 1
                THEN 'INPATIENT + PHARMACY'
            WHEN COALESCE(d.outpatient_hiv_dates, 0) >= 2
             AND COALESCE(r.pharmacy_pass, 0) = 1
                THEN 'OUTPATIENT + PHARMACY'
            WHEN COALESCE(d.inpatient_pass, 0) = 1
                THEN 'INPATIENT ONLY'
            WHEN COALESCE(d.outpatient_hiv_dates, 0) >= 2
                THEN 'OUTPATIENT ONLY'
            WHEN COALESCE(r.pharmacy_pass, 0) = 1
                THEN 'PHARMACY ONLY'
            ELSE 'NO QUALIFYING ROUTE'
        END AS hiv_route

    FROM no_art n
    LEFT JOIN work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_hiv_dx_summary d
        ON n.patient_id = d.patient_id
    LEFT JOIN work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_hiv_rx_summary r
        ON n.patient_id = r.patient_id
),
route_counts AS (
    SELECT
        hiv_route,
        COUNT(*) AS patients
    FROM routes
    GROUP BY hiv_route
)
SELECT
    hiv_route,
    patients,
    ROUND(
        100.0 * patients / SUM(patients) OVER (),
        1
    ) AS pct_patients
FROM route_counts
ORDER BY patients DESC;
  ")
```

Only 3 patients have passed 3 route WITHIN THE LAST YEAR WHICH IS WHAT WE NEEDED. 

```{r}
DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "
  WITH suspicious AS (
    SELECT
        h.patient_id,
        h.event_date AS hospice_date,
        r.latest_pharmacy_date
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_f_candidates h

    LEFT JOIN work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_art_rx_fills_12m a
        ON h.patient_id = a.patient_id

    INNER JOIN work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_hiv_rx_summary r
        ON h.patient_id = r.patient_id

    WHERE h.hiv_status = TRUE
      AND a.patient_id IS NULL
      AND COALESCE(r.pharmacy_pass, 0) = 1

      /* Route 3 evidence occurred during the adherence year */
      AND r.latest_pharmacy_date >= DATEADD(day, -365, h.event_date)
),

pharmacy_names AS (

    /* BRAND NAME */
    SELECT
        s.patient_id,
        s.hospice_date,
        s.latest_pharmacy_date,
        p.fill_date::DATE AS fill_date,
        p.days_supply,
        p.brand_name,
        p.generic_name,
        'BRAND' AS name_source,
        UPPER(TRIM(p.brand_name)) AS match_name

    FROM suspicious s

    INNER JOIN komodo_202610.pharmacy_events p
        ON s.patient_id = p.patient_id
       AND p.fill_date::DATE >= DATEADD(day, -365, s.hospice_date)
       AND p.fill_date::DATE < s.hospice_date

    WHERE p.brand_name IS NOT NULL


    UNION ALL


    /* GENERIC NAME */
    SELECT
        s.patient_id,
        s.hospice_date,
        s.latest_pharmacy_date,
        p.fill_date::DATE AS fill_date,
        p.days_supply,
        p.brand_name,
        p.generic_name,
        'GENERIC' AS name_source,
        UPPER(TRIM(p.generic_name)) AS match_name

    FROM suspicious s

    INNER JOIN komodo_202610.pharmacy_events p
        ON s.patient_id = p.patient_id
       AND p.fill_date::DATE >= DATEADD(day, -365, s.hospice_date)
       AND p.fill_date::DATE < s.hospice_date

    WHERE p.generic_name IS NOT NULL
)

SELECT
    p.patient_id,
    p.hospice_date,
    p.latest_pharmacy_date,
    p.fill_date,
    p.days_supply,

    p.brand_name,
    p.generic_name,
    p.name_source,
    p.match_name,

    CASE
        WHEN r.match_name IS NOT NULL THEN 'YES'
        ELSE 'NO'
    END AS route3_match,

    CASE
        WHEN a.match_name IS NOT NULL THEN 'YES'
        ELSE 'NO'
    END AS art_bridge_match,

    a.canonical_drug_name

FROM pharmacy_names p

LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        UPPER(TRIM(match_name)) AS match_name
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_route3_match_names
) r
    ON p.match_name = r.match_name

LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        UPPER(TRIM(match_name)) AS match_name,
        canonical_drug_name
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_art_name_bridge
) a
    ON p.match_name = a.match_name

/* only show medication names relevant to our HIV/ART logic */
WHERE r.match_name IS NOT NULL
   OR a.match_name IS NOT NULL

ORDER BY
    p.patient_id,
    p.fill_date,
    p.name_source;
  
  
  
  ")


```


The answer back is the issue is the days supply is null, so PDC cannot be calculated from these claims.  I will need to ask if these will be classified as non-calculable PDC rather than nonadherent. 

The remaining ART workflow is:
1. Convert each component interval into patient-day coverage.
2. For each patient-day, determine how many ART components are active.
3. Determine whether that day represents adequate ART coverage, using the protocol’s 2- or 3-drug regimen logic.
4. Count the number of adequately covered days.
5. Calculate:
\[
\text{PDC}=\frac{\text{days adequately covered by ART}}{365}
\]

*PDC = 0*: The patient has qualifying ART pharmacy fills with valid dates and days supplied, but never reaches your requirement of at least 2 concurrent ART components during the 365-day window.

*PDC greater than 0*: The patient has at least some days with 2 or more concurrent ART components.

*PDC = NULL*: We cannot calculate PDC from qualifying ART fills. This could be because no qualifying claims were found or because relevant prescription information was missing.( like days supply)


6. Then classify:
   - PDC < 0.80 = nonadherent
   - sensitivity at $<$0.85
   - sensitivity at $<$0.95
That mirrors Dr. Mui’s approach conceptually: PDC is based on days covered by at least two ART medications, with <80% as the primary nonadherence threshold and 85$%$/95$%$ sensitivity thresholds.

I updated the tables now. I left it like this. 
HIV+ + art_pdc_calculable = TRUE
-- PDC available 

HIV+ + art_pdc_calculable = FALSE
--- PDC could not be calculated

HIV−

I did make boosters include in the primary table. 

nonadherent_80 = 1  → nonadherent, PDC < 0.80
nonadherent_80 = 0  → adherent, PDC ≥ 0.80
nonadherent_80 = NULL → PDC not calculable / not applicable

art_pdc
→ continuous adherence measure
→ e.g. 0.732 = 73.2% of days covered

nonadherent_85 / nonadherent_95

```{r}
        COUNT(*) AS n_rows,
        COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) AS n_patients,
        SUM(CASE WHEN patient_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_patient_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN event_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_hospice_date,
        MIN(event_date) AS earliest_hospice,
        MAX(event_date) AS latest_hospice
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_f_candidates
")
poly_cohort_check
```
To clarify the defaults in nemos code were `12` months, `5` classes, and `90` days. Stage 2 so this does not decide where ART counts towards polypharmacy. 
It will:
- create each patient's 12-month pre-hospice window;
- scan pharmacy claims;
- keep paid terminal claims with valid NDC11 and positive `days_supply`;
- include carry-in fills whose medication supply overlaps the beginning of the window;
- save the cleaned pharmacy fills;
- export the unique NDC11 codes needed for mapping.

Comparing the two ART algorithms directly 
```{r}
DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,"
WITH art AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT patient_id
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_poly12m_art_exclusions_v2
),
pdc AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT patient_id
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_art_pdc_summary
)
SELECT
    CASE WHEN a.patient_id IS NOT NULL
         THEN 'ART MATCH' ELSE 'NO ART MATCH' END AS ndc_status,
    CASE WHEN p.patient_id IS NOT NULL
         THEN 'PDC RECORD' ELSE 'NO PDC RECORD' END AS pdc_status,
    COUNT(*) AS patients
FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_f_candidates h
LEFT JOIN art a ON h.patient_id = a.patient_id
LEFT JOIN pdc p ON h.patient_id = p.patient_id
WHERE h.hiv_status = TRUE
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;
  ")

```

So this means my two art identification methods agree mostly in terms of the HIV positive patients.There is an NDC record for ART butnot for my pdc. That means one patient can have an ART-associated NDC in the polypharmacy data but still lack a qualifying PDC record.interesting no pdc 576. 



```{r}
DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,"
/* find the one HIV-positive patient with an ART NDC match but NULL PDC */
WITH art_ndc_patients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        i.patient_id
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_poly12m_art_exclusions_v2 e
    JOIN work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_poly12m_index_windows i
        ON e.index_id = i.index_id
)
SELECT
    h.patient_id,
    h.event_date AS hospice_date,
    h.art_pdc
FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_f_candidates h
JOIN art_ndc_patients a
    ON h.patient_id = a.patient_id
WHERE h.hiv_status = TRUE
  AND h.art_pdc IS NULL;
    ")
```

```{r}
DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,"
WITH missing_art AS (
    SELECT p.patient_id, p.art_pdc
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_art_pdc_summary p
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT DISTINCT patient_id
        FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_poly12m_art_exclusions_v2
    ) a ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id
    WHERE a.patient_id IS NULL
),
fill_patients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT f.patient_id
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_poly12m_fills f
    JOIN missing_art m ON f.patient_id = m.patient_id
),
matching_dates AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT r.patient_id
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_art_rx_fills_12m r
    JOIN missing_art m ON r.patient_id = m.patient_id
    JOIN work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_poly12m_fills f
        ON r.patient_id = f.patient_id
       AND r.fill_date = f.fill_date
)
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN f.patient_id IS NULL THEN 'No pharmacy fills'
        WHEN d.patient_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Matching fill dates'
        ELSE 'No matching ART dates'
    END AS category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT m.patient_id) AS patients,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.art_pdc > 0
        THEN m.patient_id END) AS positive_pdc,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.art_pdc = 0
        THEN m.patient_id END) AS zero_pdc
FROM missing_art m
LEFT JOIN fill_patients f ON m.patient_id = f.patient_id
LEFT JOIN matching_dates d ON m.patient_id = d.patient_id
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
")
```

# stage 3 
After validating the exclusions, the next task is to modify 3_build_polypharmacy_exposures.R so the exposure calculation excludes records found in hospice_poly12m_art_exclusions.I will keep the orignal ATC crosswalk and calculate :
$$
Non-ART \space polypharmacy  = \left\{
\begin{aligned}
  1, & \quad \text{if } 5+ \text{concurrent non-ART ATC3 classes for 90+ days } \\
  0,       & \quad \text{otherwise}
\end{aligned}
\right.
$$
HIV Route 3 identification: Vemlidy remains excluded.
ART proportion of days covered (PDC): Vemlidy remains excluded.
Non-ART polypharmacy: Vemlidy remains eligible, provided it has a valid Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) class mapping.

now for polypharmacy exclusions:
Medication category                                                               	Non-ART polypharmacy
Identified HIV treatment products, such as Biktarvy and Triumeq	                         Exclude
ART combination products, such as Descovy and Truvada	                        Exclude under the current rule
Vemlidy                                                                                 	Include
Other medications not matched to my ART exclusion reference	Include if they have a qualifying ATC mapping

To reiterate - Vemlidy's verified National Drug Code (NDC) is 61958230101.which makes it a hep B treatment.

I added this to a .gitignore as it is just so large. Now I will match the 200 NDCs to the FDA json file 

```{r}
unmapped <- dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT priority_rank, ndc11, fill_records
    FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.unmapped_stage3_ndcs
    ORDER BY priority_rank
")
unmapped$ndc11 <- as.character(unmapped$ndc11)
# read the FDA JSON locally
fda <- fromJSON("polypharmacy/drug-ndc-0001-of-0001.json",simplifyVector = FALSE)
# convert FDA package codes into NDC11
to_ndc11 <- function(code) {
    if (is.null(code) || length(code) == 0) return(NA_character_)
    code <- as.character(code[1])
    if (is.na(code)) return(NA_character_)
    if (grepl("^[0-9]{11}$", code)) return(code)
    p <- strsplit(code, "-", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    if (length(p) != 3) return(NA_character_)
    fmt <- paste(nchar(p), collapse = "-")
    if (fmt == "4-4-2") return(paste0("0", p[1], p[2], p[3]))
    if (fmt == "5-3-2") return(paste0(p[1], "0", p[2], p[3]))
    if (fmt == "5-4-1") return(paste0(p[1], p[2], "0", p[3]))
    if (fmt == "5-4-2") return(paste0(p, collapse = ""))
    NA_character_
}
# match NDC11 to the FDA brand and generic names
matches <- list()
for (drug in fda$results) {
    if (is.null(drug$packaging)) next
    codes <- unique(vapply(drug$packaging, function(p) {
        to_ndc11(p$package_ndc)
    }, character(1)))
    hits <- intersect(codes[!is.na(codes)], unmapped$ndc11)
    if (!length(hits)) next
    for (ndc in hits) {
        matches[[length(matches) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
            ndc11 = ndc,
            brand_name = if (is.null(drug$brand_name)) NA_character_
                         else as.character(drug$brand_name[1]),
            generic_name = if (is.null(drug$generic_name)) NA_character_
                           else as.character(drug$generic_name[1])
        )
    }
}
# combine FDA information with the existing table
identified <- if (length(matches)) {
    unique(do.call(rbind, matches))
} else {
    data.frame(ndc11 = character(), brand_name = character(),
               generic_name = character())
}
review <- unmapped
review$brand_name <- NA_character_
review$generic_name <- NA_character_
review$fda_match_status <- "NOT_FOUND"
for (i in seq_len(nrow(review))) {
    x <- identified[identified$ndc11 == review$ndc11[i], ]
    if (nrow(x) == 1) {
        review$brand_name[i] <- x$brand_name
        review$generic_name[i] <- x$generic_name
        review$fda_match_status[i] <- "MATCHED"
    } else if (nrow(x) > 1) {
        review$fda_match_status[i] <- "MULTIPLE_MATCHES"
    }
}
# Validate before writing to Redshift
stopifnot(nrow(review) == 200)
print(table(review$fda_match_status))
#create the new bridge table
target <- "work_rohanramirez_a299.bridging_unmapped_ndcs"
DatabaseConnector::executeSql(con, paste0("
    DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ", target, ";
    CREATE TABLE ", target, " (
        priority_rank INTEGER,
        ndc11 VARCHAR(11),
        fill_records BIGINT,
        brand_name VARCHAR(2048),
        generic_name VARCHAR(2048),
        fda_match_status VARCHAR(32)
    ) DISTSTYLE ALL SORTKEY(priority_rank);
"), progressBar = FALSE, reportOverallTime = FALSE)
# insert the 200 matched records
quote_sql <- function(x) {
    if (is.na(x)) return("NULL")
    paste0("'", gsub("'", "''", as.character(x), fixed = TRUE), "'")
}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(review))) {
    values <- c(
        as.character(review$priority_rank[i]),
        quote_sql(review$ndc11[i]),
        as.character(review$fill_records[i]),
        quote_sql(review$brand_name[i]),
        quote_sql(review$generic_name[i]),
        quote_sql(review$fda_match_status[i])
    )
    sql <- paste0("INSERT INTO ", target, " VALUES (",
                  paste(values, collapse = ", "), ");")
    DatabaseConnector::executeSql(con, sql,
        progressBar = FALSE, reportOverallTime = FALSE)
}
rm(fda)
gc()
cat("Bridge created with", nrow(review), "NDCs\n")
```

```{r}
# Pull ART coverage results for HIV-positive hospice patients
art_data <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "

      h.art_pdc::DOUBLE PRECISION AS art_pdc,
      h.art_pdc_calculable,
      h.nonadherent_80,
      h.nonadherent_85,
      h.nonadherent_95,
      p.days_covered_2plus
  FROM work_rohanramirez_a299.hospice_f_candidates h
  LEFT JOIN work_rohanramirez_a299.hiv_art_pdc_summary p
      ON h.patient_id = p.patient_id
  WHERE h.hiv_status = TRUE
")

# Keep only patients with calculable ART PDC
art_plot <- art_data %>%
  filter(art_pdc_calculable == TRUE, !is.na(art_pdc)) %>%
  mutate(
    pdc_percent = 100 * art_pdc,
    pdc_hist = pmin(pdc_percent, 99.999),
    coverage_group = ifelse(art_pdc < 0.80,
                            "Below 80%", "80% or above")
  )


# Descriptive statistics for the figure
art_stats <- art_plot %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_pdc = mean(art_pdc),
    sd_pdc = sd(art_pdc),
    median_pdc = median(art_pdc),
    q1 = quantile(art_pdc, 0.25),
    q3 = quantile(art_pdc, 0.75),
    mean_covered_days = mean(days_covered_2plus, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_covered_days = sd(days_covered_2plus, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_covered_days = median(days_covered_2plus, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_below_80 = sum(art_pdc < 0.80),
    pct_below_80 = 100 * mean(art_pdc < 0.80)
  )
```
